title: Group the currently owner-authorized Command Work Queue by type or status without new routes or data providers
goal: Close the canonical CAP-CMD-101 §11/§25 manual grouping gap by grouping all currently authorized, filtered Incident and Task rows before stable 50-item cursor pagination, reusing one existing Command route and first-party owner ACLs.
invariants: The product owner is Command CAP-CMD-101; the Git base is parent draft PR #171, NOT the canonical work parent (epic E10-CMD-101).
Only exact existing owner-sourced `Kind` or `Status` are grouping keys. Do not invent priority/severity, add a new source, mutate owner assignment or perform Class-2 operations.

Authorize each in-scope Incident or Task with the current host principal, tenant, environment and owner.CanRead BEFORE grouping and before obtaining source freshness; denied/cross-tenant records never influence groups.

Grouping happens on the entire authorized filtered bounded cohort before stable cursor paging; group then existing chronological sort, stable kind/ID ties. Page breaks may repeat a group title but do not change membership.
The opaque cursor digest binds the group key, full freshly authorized rows and prior filters; current-page selection and navigation preserve grouping and reauthorize on every request.
Exactly six Command system views remain configurations of the same GET route. Shared Saved Views persistence and OPEN-013 mutations remain outside this task.
security_properties: Untrusted `group` accepts only `type` or `status`, one parameter, before host session/owner lookup; omission preserves historical result.
No direct client-provided principal, tenant, environment or ACL; grouping never grants authority, leaks denied group counts, or makes stale cursor usable.
Native HTML escapes owner-sourced group labels and preserves the existing strict CSP, no external dependency.

migration.rationale: Optional read-only projection field and query parameter with backward-compatible ungrouped default; no object schema/storage or Saved View definition changed.

rollback.strategy: Revert opt-in grouping and cursor group digest without touching the prior authorized filter/sort/pagination implementation.
verification: Existing owner filtering, six views, selected row and cursor/revocation tests continue passing.

inputs: CAP-CMD-101 full 27-section canonical sheet §§3,11,12,16,17,18,21,25,26 and Incidents and Work Queue module ownership; Command saved-views six-key catalogue; Incident/Task canonical objects and tenant/security/pagination contracts.
Current parent PR #171 head 54332f6443cc4592a6cd7a6a6f9dd92164f849ff, both Command and engineering workflows completed SUCCESS, DRAFT/not merged.
The prior Command queue already implements post-owner-ACL exact status/owner filters, chronological order, owner-revocation-aware 50-row cursor, row selection and native browser; grouping is absent.
outputs: Existing GET /command/work-queue supports optional `group=type|status`, aggregates no new source data, and sorts grouped authorized rows before bounded paging.
Native HTML shows group headings over current page, preserves group across view links/pagination/selection; JSON returns `group_by` only when selected.
Changing grouping or revoking visible rows invalidates existing page cursors without disclosure; old requests remain ungrouped.
acceptance_tests: With 123 authorized Task objects, 45 closed and 78 open, group=status sorts whole set and paginates as 50/50/23 without duplicates/missing rows, retaining chronological order within groups.

Native grouped page 2 renders group heading and preserves group context through the exact selected current page; invalidated/revoked owner authorization causes generic 404 rather than showing stale rows.
Grouping by type includes only readable Incident and Task rows and does not call ACL on foreign tenant objects. Group labels in HTML remain escaped.
Unknown or duplicate group query, untrusted owner/tenant injection, and unsupported direct projection fail before host session or owner.CanRead. No group keeps historical response.
GitHub exact-head command-work-queue-runtime Linux/macOS/Windows and engineering-kernel including unchanged 90% security floor and SAST must pass. No merge/acceptance from green child alone.

performance_budget.rationale: Single string comparison for the selected group on already materialized bounded authorized rows; no new source lookups or network calls.
metrics: Existing <=5000 owner candidates and <=50 visible rows per page; O(n log n) deterministic sort remains, no second walk of owner graph.
No new Owner.List/CanRead calls per request; unchanged cursor digest over authorized rows.

definition_of_ready: E10-CMD-101K-OWNERFILTER implemented on PR #171, SHA 54332f6443cc4592a6cd7a6a6f9dd92164f849ff, its exact-HEAD Command and engineering Actions SUCCESS; PR remains DRAFT and unmerged.
CAP-CMD-101 §11 explicitly requires manual grouping and Class-0 filters/sort; `Kind` and `Status` are existing Command Item fields; no OPEN product decision required for narrow read-only opt-in.
One bounded Command context, <=4 executable/non-test files and no independent migration or new security model.
definition_of_done: Publish scoped code/tests and this manifest to a separate child PR preserving parent #171 SHA and all previously audited commits.
On exact child HEAD GitHub Actions verify all mandatory checks; record evidence and only mark this task IMPLEMENTED if the code is actually published/tested.
Neither CAP-CMD-101 acceptance nor production delivery nor approval of unmerged parent PRs is asserted; arrange one independent read-only L2 for this material UI+pagination integration.
